result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in File & Path Security: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Static assessment restricted to eShopLegacyMVCSolution; reviewed both controller implementations, catalog binding/model validation, service persistence, routes, filters, initialization file access, and XML/upload sinks.
No running deployment or exploit execution. Findings describe one arbitrary-file-read vulnerability under three related CWE classifications, not three independent vulnerabilities.

PictureFileName has no filename/confinement validation. Antiforgery protects catalog POSTs from CSRF, not malicious direct clients; a client can obtain its own token. Initializer paths are application-controlled local inputs. No application XML parser or upload entry point was identified.
Execution duration was not measured. Timestamp records overall assessment completion.

values.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
values.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: CatalogController.Create/Edit bind attacker-supplied PictureFileName and persist it without confinement validation. PicController.Index combines the stored name with ~/Pics at lines 38-39, reads all bytes at line 44, and returns them at line 46. A client can submit a valid catalog entry with ../Web.config, then request its picture to retrieve application configuration readable by the worker identity. CatalogServiceMock likewise stores submitted objects. No application authorization filter protects catalog actions; antiforgery does not restrict a direct client with its own token. No extension allowlist guards the read; unknown extensions are returned as application/octet-stream. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH arbitrary file disclosure.

values.name: Relative Path Traversal
values.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: Same arbitrary-file-read issue as CWE-22: PictureFileName is writable through catalog Create/Edit, and PicController.Index passes a relative traversal such as ../Web.config through Path.Combine directly into File.ReadAllBytes at line 44. There is no canonical-path containment check or filename restriction. Access is limited only by the application process file permissions. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH.

values.name: Absolute Path Traversal
values.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: Same arbitrary-file-read issue as CWE-22: catalog Create/Edit accept absolute PictureFileName values, including Windows drive-rooted paths. Path.Combine(webRoot, item.PictureFileName) discards webRoot when its second argument is rooted; File.ReadAllBytes and File return the targeted file. No rooted-path rejection or containment check exists. An attacker can retrieve any known file readable by the worker identity. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH.

values.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
values.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

values.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
values.description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.
